title: enhanced-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback-workflows
author: Nora Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve safety and observability for canary + A/B + shadow rollouts by making the autorollback workflows more robust to noisy metrics and transient infra failures. This PR adds quorumed metric evaluation, per-stage stability windows, and probe-based quarantine to prevent spurious rollbacks while preserving fast rollback for true regressions.

Summary of changes: 1) Add a metric-quorum evaluator that requires a configurable fraction of metrics to breach thresholds before triggering a rollback. 2) Introduce per-stage stability windows (min-stable-duration) so short, transient degradations do not immediately flip the rollback state. 3) Add probing/quarantine stage: when a threshold is breached, traffic is moved to a probing cohort and a targeted probe set is run to confirm regression before rollback. 4) Extend observability: new telemetry for quorum state, probe pass/fail, and stage transition reasons; dashboards and alerting docs updated. 5) E2E tests: new harness tests that simulate transient spikes and real regressions to validate no false positives and timely rollback on real degradations.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric quorum evaluator implemented (core engine)
- [x] Per-stage stability windows implemented and plumbed through rollout configs
- [x] Probing/quarantine stage and probe runner
- [x] Telemetry events and metrics (quorum_state, probe_result, stage_transition_reason)
- [x] Console dashboard and alert docs updated (docs/rollouts/quorum.md)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] E2E simulation tests added to perf-canary harness
- [x] Backwards compatible config (defaults preserve current behaviour)

Design notes: The quorum evaluator treats each configured SLO/metric as a vote; a rollback is only triggered when >= quorum_fraction of metrics are in a breach state for the configured evaluation window. We keep a fast-fail path for high-severity runtime errors (e.g., model OOM or invalid responses) which still trigger immediate rollback. Stability windows are applied per rollout stage: canary stages default to shorter windows, shadow stages default to longer windows. The probe runner executes a small set of golden prompts and synthetic load patterns against the canary variant to confirm regressions. Probe failures increment a probe-failure counter and only after N failures do we mark the probe as failed.

Compatibility: All rollout specs are backward-compatible; new quorum, stability_window, and probe_* fields are optional. Default values mimic today's autorollback behavior.

Risks and mitigations: Quorum thresholds set too high could delay real rollbacks - default is conservative (0.5) and ops can tune per-customer. Probe suite false negatives would delay rollback; probes are prioritized by production failure modes and we added a mechanism to mark high-confidence probes.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the quorum evaluator correctness, the probe runner isolation (no leakage to production traffic), and observability events (are transition reasons sufficiently descriptive).

Related: ENG-1423 (rollout reliability), ENG-1688 (rollback observability).

release_notes: Enhance autorollback workflows: metric quorum evaluation, per-stage stability windows, probe/quarantine stage, added telemetry and e2e tests. Backwards-compatible rollout config additions; ops can tune quorum/stability/probe parameters.
discussion_summary: Reviewers focused on safety (probe isolation), correctness of quorum voting semantics, and telemetry tags. All concerns addressed; tests added for NaN metrics and probe retry/backoff. Merged via squash after approvals.
notes: This PR follows ENG-1423 and ENG-1688. Customers on Dedicated who have custom rollout configs should review new optional fields; no automatic changes to existing specs.
